title: Nur Jahan
summary: Mehr-un-Nissa, granted the title Nur Jahan ("Light of the World") by Emperor Jahangir upon their marriage in 1611, was the twentieth and chief wife of the fourth Mughal emperor. A skilled politician and diplomat, she exercised unprecedented executive power during Jahangir's reign, issuing imperial decrees and becoming the only Mughal queen to have coins minted in her name. She was also a patron of architecture, commissioning the tomb of I'timad al-Daula in Agra.

uncertainty.note: Range spans her marriage to Emperor Jahangir and period of imperial co-rule until his death in 1627; she lived c. 1577–1645.
